chief_complaint: new tiny red spots on my legs and heavy bleeding from gums
hpi_details: 35F presents with sudden onset of a non-blanching pinpoint red rash (petechiae) on her lower legs. She noticed her gums bleeding profusely after brushing her teeth. She had a severe viral upper respiratory infection 2 weeks ago.
ideas: thinks she has a blood disorder

investigation_events.title: STAT thrombocytopenia results
investigation_events.availability_message: The STAT platelet count and smear are now available; bleeding precautions and urgent hematology involvement should not be delayed.

results.value: Marked thrombocytopenia with occasional large platelets; no schistocytes or blasts

core_concepts: ITP involves IgG antibodies targeting platelets for destruction in the spleen.
Presents with isolated severe thrombocytopenia (no anemia or leukopenia).
common_misconceptions: Assuming a coagulation factor defect (PT/aPTT will be normal in ITP).
dangerous_errors: Discharging a patient with severe thrombocytopenia (<10k) due to risk of intracranial hemorrhage.
management_principles: Corticosteroids, IVIG, hematology consult. Avoid NSAIDs and trauma.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: UpToDate & National Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guidelines 2026

reference_soap.subjective: 35F with sudden petechiae and gingival bleeding following a viral illness.
reference_soap.objective: Widespread petechiae on bilateral lower extremities. Blood in oral cavity. Hemodynamically stable.
reference_soap.plan: STAT CBC, peripheral smear. Avoid NSAIDs. Hematology consult for possible IVIG and steroids.

learning_objectives: Identify clinical signs of severe thrombocytopenia (petechiae, mucosal bleeding).

teaching.one_liner: Sudden onset of petechiae and mucosal bleeding following a viral infection, indicative of ITP.

must_ask.say: When did you first notice the tiny red spots on your legs and the gum bleeding?
Have you had a cold, flu, or any other viral infection in the past few weeks?
Have you noticed any other unusual bruising, nosebleeds, or blood in your urine or stool?
Are you taking any new medications, aspirin, or blood thinners?
Have you had any severe headache, confusion, or vision changes?

history.answer: I woke up yesterday and noticed tiny red spots all over my lower legs, and when I brushed my teeth this morning, my gums started bleeding heavily and would not stop.
The red spots appeared abruptly yesterday morning on both of my lower legs without any bump or fall, and they have not faded.
They are tiny pinpoint flat red dots that do not fade when pressed, and I have not had any large spreading bruises or swollen bumps in my muscles.
My gums started bleeding profusely as soon as I brushed this morning and kept oozing for over an hour, though I have not had nosebleeds or bleeding from small skin cuts.
My last period ended about ten days ago and was normal, so I have not noticed heavier flow or unusual clots yet.
No, my urine looks normal yellow, and my bowel movements are regular brown without any black tarry color or red blood.
No, I have not vomited blood, thrown up dark coffee-ground material, or coughed up blood.
No, I feel completely clear-headed and have no headache, dizziness, visual blurring, weakness, or numbness.
No, I had my wisdom teeth pulled a few years back and had no abnormal bleeding or delayed clotting after the procedure.
No, I do not have a fever, chills, night sweats, or frequent infections.
No, I have not felt unusually exhausted, pale, short of breath, or experienced bone pain or unexplained weight loss.
I had a bad viral cold with a runny nose, mild fever, and sore throat about two weeks ago, but it cleared up completely after a few days.
No, I have not started any new prescription drugs, antibiotics, or received injections like heparin recently.
No, I do not take aspirin, pain relievers like ibuprofen, blood thinners, steroids, or dietary supplements like ginkgo or omega-3.
No, I have never had liver disease or hepatitis, my eyes are not yellow, and my belly has not swollen.
I eat three regular, balanced meals a day with plenty of vegetables and fruits, and I do not have chronic diarrhea or digestive issues.
No, the spots are smooth and flat rather than raised, and my joints and stomach feel completely fine.
No one in my family has hemophilia, von Willebrand disease, or any tendency to bleed or bruise easily.
No, nobody has hurt or struck me, and I feel completely safe at home with my husband.
I am terrified that I might have some kind of serious blood disorder that is making my blood fail to clot.
I was terrified by how much my gums bled, and I am worried I could suddenly start bleeding internally into my organs or head.
I want to get a complete blood test done immediately so we can figure out what is wrong and stop the bleeding.
I have never had any chronic medical conditions or health problems in the past.
I have never been hospitalized or had surgery, other than having my wisdom teeth extracted.
I do not take any regular prescription medications or over-the-counter medicines.
I have no known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used tobacco products.
I only drink a glass of wine on rare social occasions, maybe once a month.
I work as an office accountant and live with my husband in a quiet apartment.
My last menstrual period began ten days ago and was normal. We use condoms for birth control, and there is no possibility that I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 120/78 mmHg, heart rate is 74 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, body temperature is 36.7°C, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Alert, oriented woman appearing anxious but in no acute cardiopulmonary distress.
Pink conjunctivae without pallor or petechiae, and white sclerae without jaundice.
Active minor oozing and dried blood along the gingival margins, with no oral mucosal blood blisters or palate petechiae.
No cervical, supraclavicular, or submandibular lymphadenopathy palpable.
Flat, symmetrical abdomen without distension, visible veins, or spider angiomas.
Abdomen is soft and non-tender, with no palpable hepatomegaly or splenomegaly.
Dense, non-blanching, non-palpable pinpoint petechiae covering both lower legs and ankles, with no large ecchymoses.
Both knees and ankles have full range of motion without swelling, effusion, warmth, or tenderness.
Cranial nerves II through XII are intact, pupils are equal and reactive, and there are no focal deficits.
